# PGTune

> PGTune is a free, open source web tool, which suggests PostgreSQL configuration for given hardware and workload: PostgreSQL version, operating system, type of application, RAM, number of CPUs and connections, storage type and data size. The result is a list of `postgresql.conf` settings or `ALTER SYSTEM` commands with explanations of possible risks.

PGTune follows the "do no harm" principle: generated settings should not make a database worse than PostgreSQL defaults. Settings, which equal PostgreSQL defaults for the selected version, are omitted. Settings, which may prevent PostgreSQL from starting on some builds or systems (`wal_compression = lz4`, `io_method = io_uring`, `wal_level = minimal`), come with a warning and a command to check support. The result is a starting point, not a final tuning: queries, data size and number of clients of real application also matter, so apply it on a test or staging server first and monitor the database after the change.

Configuration is calculated in the browser by JavaScript, nothing is sent to a server. The page is described completely by its URL parameters, so a configuration can be shared or generated by a link, for example:

https://pgtune.leopard.in.ua/?dbVersion=18&osType=linux&dbType=web&cpuNum=8&totalMemory=16&totalMemoryUnit=GB&connectionNum=&hdType=ssd&dbSize=mid_ram

URL parameters (all of them are required, except `cpuNum` and `connectionNum`, which can be empty; if any parameter is invalid, the empty form is shown):

- `dbVersion`: PostgreSQL version, `10` to `19`
- `osType`: `linux`, `windows` or `mac`
- `dbType`: type of application: `web` (many short, simple queries, mostly reads), `oltp` (many concurrent short transactions with frequent writes), `dw` (data warehouse: few long analytical queries over large amounts of data, bulk loads), `desktop` (PostgreSQL shares the computer with other programs and uses little memory) or `mixed` (both short transactions and heavy analytical queries)
- `totalMemory` and `totalMemoryUnit`: RAM available to PostgreSQL, a whole number with unit `MB`, `GB` or `TB` (at least 512 MB)
- `cpuNum`: number of CPUs, which PostgreSQL can use (optional)
- `connectionNum`: expected maximum number of connections, 20 to 260000 (optional; if empty, it is assumed from the type of application: 200 for web, 300 for oltp, 100 for others, lower if it does not fit in memory, but never below 100)
- `hdType`: data storage: `nvme`, `ssd`, `san` (network storage) or `hdd`
- `dbSize`: total data size compared to RAM: `less_ram`, `mid_ram` (1x to 3x RAM) or `greater_ram` (more than 3x RAM)

The HTML of the page is prerendered without parameters, so it contains only the empty form: to read a generated configuration, open the link in a browser with JavaScript or use the calculation code from the repository. Generated settings include memory (`shared_buffers`, `effective_cache_size`, `work_mem`, `maintenance_work_mem`), WAL and checkpoints, planner costs, I/O concurrency and asynchronous I/O (PostgreSQL 18+), parallel workers, autovacuum and connections. Settings, which take effect only after restart, are marked as "restart required". Warnings are grouped as "may prevent startup", "memory risk" and "note", and are included as comments in the copied configuration.

## Docs

- [How it works](https://pgtune.leopard.in.ua/about): principles of PGTune, how to choose type of application and what to check before applying the configuration
- [README](https://github.com/le0pard/pgtune/blob/master/README.md): development, tests and contributing

## Source code

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/le0pard/pgtune): source code, issues and pull requests (MIT license)
- [Calculation of settings and warnings](https://github.com/le0pard/pgtune/blob/master/src/features/configuration/configurationSelectors.js): formulas for every generated setting, with reasons in comments
- [Example configurations](https://github.com/le0pard/pgtune/tree/master/src/features/configuration/__tests__/__snapshots__/configurations): generated output for representative inputs of each PostgreSQL version, operating system, application type and storage

## Optional

- [PostgreSQL: Server Configuration](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config.html): official documentation of all PostgreSQL settings
- [PostgreSQL: Resource Consumption](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-resource.html): memory, disk, asynchronous I/O and parallel worker settings
